the_ruling_verbatim:
so question:   One default you can flip. The PROVEME to PROVED gate requires hollow evidence for code-seams. Saying nope makes it advisory.
Gates are supposed to be hard, deterministic, state changes. no hollow evidence. that sounds like a bug.
I AM SO RULING IT RIGHT NOW
now_the_spec_says: A gate is a hard, deterministic state change. It has no advisory mode and no switch; a missing input (no hollow evidence, no seal) is the gate's red, never a reason to soften it. Offering a flip on a gate is the defect.
context: CC's handoff message before the restart offered 'one default you can flip: the PROVEME->PROVED gate requires evidence.hollow for code-seams; saying nope makes it advisory'. Akien read it as a bug. Standing ruling 2026-08-10-clearance-is-mandatory had already answered MANDATORY to the literal question mandatory-or-advisory; this ruling generalises it from clearance to every gate. Conformance landed in CairnCommons 1225cda before intake (both tickets carry an `amended` record with his words); as_of points the baseline at 886c9ba, the commit before that correction. CC memory gates-are-hard-never-advisory records the failure mode.
